material_events_in_window: Form 990 filed Jul 15 2024 (LA Jewish Home For The Aging): Revenue $34.58M, Expenses $50.72M, NET INCOME -$16.14M, NET ASSETS -$79.01M. Negative-equity going-concern signal.
CCN 055013 Eisenberg Village (166 SNF beds, Reseda): 4-star Overall, 3-star Health Inspection, 4-star Staffing, 5-star QM. 1 fine totaling $30,744 (May 2026 file).
CCN 555846 Joyce Eisenberg-Keefer Medical Center D/P SNF (Grancell, 344 SNF beds, Reseda): 5-star Overall, 3-star Health Inspection, 5-star Staffing, 5-star QM. Zero fines.
2024: LA Jewish Health awarded $28M from California Department of Health Care Services (one-time grant; not a credit event but liquidity support).
Insured rating carry-forward AA reflects Cal-Mortgage wrap, not underlying credit which appears strained per Form 990.
verified_outcome.outcome_class_rationale: Material event: FY2024 Form 990 showed -$16M operating loss and -$79M total net assets (negative equity). This is a going-concern flag. CMS facility-level ratings remain 4-5 star, so SNF detector does not fire. But the GOING_CONCERN_ALPHA detector should fire from the 990. Insured rating carry-forward masks underlying distress; if it weren't insured, this would be a downgrade.

nh_cms_star_rating.source_data: CMS Provider Info May 2026 — using larger of two campuses (Grancell CCN 555846, 344 beds). Eisenberg (055013, 166 beds) is 4-star Overall.
nh_cms_star_rating._note: Weighted by bed count, system is approximately 4.7-star Overall.

nh_civil_monetary_penalty.source_data: Aggregated across both campuses: Eisenberg 1 fine $30,744; Grancell 0 fines. Total $30,744.

operating_metrics._note: Form 990 revenue ($34.6M) does not match ~$175M operating revenue — 990 likely covers Eisenberg subsidiary entity only, not full LAJHA consolidated. But negative net assets of -$79M is a confirmed Form 990 line.

going_concern.evidence: FY2024 Form 990 Eisenberg subsidiary: -$16.1M net income, -$79.0M net assets. Negative equity is a substantial doubt indicator.
going_concern._note: Not a formal auditor going-concern paragraph; inferred from balance-sheet impairment.
